Sarcoma sinoviale della regione antero-l: Synovial sarcoma of the anterolateral region of the right hip
Donna di 34 anni. Tumefazione palpabile: 34-year-old woman. Palpable swelling of the lateral region of the right hip, grown over the last few months. MRI of the pelvis and proximal thighs (available sequences: axial T1 and STIR; without contrast).
Il sarcoma sinoviale colpisce soprattutt:
Synovial sarcoma mainly affects adolescents and young adults (15-40 years), usually in the lower limbs. The name is misleading: it does not arise from the synovium and is almost never inside a joint; it is often found near joints, tendons or bursae.
On MRI it is typically a lobulated, heterogeneous mass; on T2 it may show the "triple signal" (areas hyperintense like fluid, intermediate like fat, hypointense like fibrous tissue), sometimes with fluid-fluid levels. In about one third of cases there are calcifications (better seen on X-ray or CT). It can grow slowly and have well-defined margins: a "quiet" appearance does not exclude it.
Rule of thumb for soft-tissue masses: larger than 5 cm, deep to the fascia, growing or painful (any one of these features is enough) → treat it as a sarcoma until proven otherwise. Even a superficial mass, like this one, is not reassuring if it exceeds 5 cm, with biopsy at the center that will perform the surgery (the biopsy tract must be removed together with the tumor). Staging with chest CT (lung metastases).
Massa dei tessuti molli oltre 5 cm, prof: Soft-tissue mass larger than 5 cm, deep or growing (even just one of these): sarcoma until proven otherwise.
Sarcoma sinoviale, grado intermedio (dat: Synovial sarcoma, intermediate grade (clinical data from the Soft-tissue-Sarcoma collection). Treated with radiotherapy and surgery; disease-free at last follow-up (about 1 year and 9 months).
